title: Iowa cross country prepares for final regular season race at Bradley Pink Classic
text:
← Back to the wire
Iowa cross country prepares for final regular season race at Bradley Pink Classic
Iowa cross country heads to Peoria for its final regular-season meet at the Bradley Pink Classic on Oct. 14 before turning attention to postseason competition later this month.
Iowa cross country will travel to Peoria, Illinois, for the Bradley Pink Classic on Oct. 14. The event marks the team's final race of the regular season, with the men’s 8,000-meter race scheduled for 1:30 p.m., followed by the women’s 6,000 meters at Newman Golf Club.
In their previous outing at the Gans Creek Classic, fifth-year Miriam Sandeen led Iowa's women in the 6,000 meters with a season-best time of 21:02.6 and finished 76th overall. Third-years Elena Torres and Hillary Trainor also recorded season-best times of 21:17.0 and 21:17.9, respectively. Freshman Avery Rump set a personal best with a time of 21:53.5, while third-year Julia Gehl (21:55.4) and first-year Noella Ross (22:16.7) achieved new personal records as well; collectively, the women's team placed 25th with 599 points.
On the men's side at Gans Creek Classic, third-year Kyle Montgomery finished in 57th place in the 8,000 meters with a personal record of 23:56.1 and was joined by fourth-year Luke Knepp (24:27.9), fifth-year Will Ryan (24:35.8), first-year Slader Buckheister (24:44.3), and second-year Elias Arbuckle (25:00.3) in scoring positions; several underclassmen posted additional personal bests as Iowa secured a 24th-place finish with 592 points.
This meet marks Iowa's return to Peoria after last competing in the Bradley Pink Classic in 2024 when the men placed third and women tenth overall; current runners Montgomery, Miles Wilson, Will Ryan, Sandeen, Torres, and Trainor all have prior experience at this venue.
Among top performers this season are Hillary Trainor—named to the Big Ten Runners to Watch list—who won this year’s Hawkeye Invite women's race with a personal best; Sandeen has led Iowa in multiple meets while Torres finished first among Hawkeyes throughout last season and earned conference honors.
Looking ahead following Friday's races at Peoria, Iowa will prepare for postseason competition beginning with Big Ten Championships on Oct. 30 in Madison.
